post.title: Why unspent FSA money can vanish after December 31
post.ig:
For many workers, unspent FSA money vanishes after December 31.

EBRI found about half of FSA holders forfeited money in 2022; the average forfeit was $441.
Employers can add ONE fix, never both: a carryover (up to $680 for 2026 plan years, IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32) or a grace period of up to 2.5 months.
Example: $3,400 in (2026 max), $900 left. Carryover: $680 rolls over, $220 lost. Full grace period: $0 lost if spent by March 15 (calendar-year plan).
HSAs work differently: the balance rolls over every year and stays yours (IRS Pub. 969).

Sources: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32, IRS Notice 2013-71, IRS Publication 969, EBRI (2022 FSA data, published 2024). Plans differ; check plan documents.
News and education, not financial advice.
